title: Does an oscillating source lower the Strauss exponent?
results: Bound p_c<=1+sqrt2 is correct: John/Zhou iteration uses only |F(u)|<=C|u|^p and |F(u)-F(v)|<=C(|u|+|v|)^{p-1}|u-v|, both hold for g(t)|u|^p. The 'resonance predicts 2' heuristic (exp of int t^{1-p}) is arithmetically right but not an argument; a normal-form attempt (H''=g) just recycles the oscillating factor, so nothing is proved.
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.28389 (2026 preprint): cited background on Strauss-type problems with time-dependent coefficients; the statement does not depend on it.
plain: For the 3D wave equation with source |u|^p, small smooth data give global solutions exactly when p > 1+√2 (Strauss). Multiply the source by a factor that oscillates periodically in time with average zero, such as cos t. The global-existence proof still works above 1+√2. Every blow-up proof below it breaks, because they all need the source to be positive. Is the true threshold strictly smaller?
math: Let $g$ be smooth, $2\pi$-periodic, $\int_0^{2\pi}g=0$, $g\not\equiv0$ (model $g=\cos t$). For $u_{tt}-\Delta u=g(t)|u|^p$ on $\mathbb R^{1+3}$ with data $\varepsilon(f,h)$, $f,h\in C_c^\infty$ (solutions in the usual weak/mild sense, e.g. $C([0,T);H^1)$ with John-type weighted bounds), let $p_c(g)=\inf\{p>1:\forall f,h\ \exists\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the solution is global for all $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0\}$. Since John/Zhou/Glassey global existence uses only $|g|u|^p|\lesssim|u|^p$ and the matching Lipschitz bound, $p_c(g)\le1+\sqrt2$. Is $p_c(g)<1+\sqrt2$? Determine $p_c(g)$ and whether it depends on $g$ (a heuristic predicts 2). For $1<p<p_c(g)$, determine the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$ for suitable data.
lean_gap: Statement left as sorry by design.
